tasks.//check: Everything Deno can type. It used to exclude `server/main.ts` — the KPS wiring, which needs `--node-modules-dir=manual` and had a `check:serve` of its own that the gate never ran — and it never mentioned `desktop/` or `tools/` at all. The rest of `web/src` is browser code and is checked by `tsc` in `web:build`, which is in the gate.
tasks.//icons: Redraws web/public/*.png. `tools/icons_test.ts` asserts the committed files match, so run this after changing the mark and commit both.
tasks.test: deno test --allow-read=. --allow-write=.tmp --allow-run=git shared/ server/ web/src/ tools/repo_test.ts tools/icons_test.ts
tasks.//test: `--allow-read=.` is for the two guards in web/src/idb_test.ts, which read the sources they are asserting about. It is the process floor; those tests narrow it again with their own `permissions` block, and every other test still runs with nothing.
tasks.//fmt: Always this, never `deno fmt <path under web/>`: given a path inside web/, Deno finds web/package.json first, ignores this file, and reformats at the default width instead of lineWidth 100 -- so the gate then rejects what fmt just wrote.
tasks.gate: deno fmt --check && deno lint && deno task check && deno task test && deno task web:build && deno task test:bundle
tasks.//serve: 27.25 -- no `-A`, and every flag here is answerable. read/write: the data directory, which holds the database, the note audio, the issued PDFs and the KPS keypair; read also `./node_modules` because the KPS client is an npm package loaded at runtime. net: unscoped, and this is the one that cannot be narrowed -- WebRTC binds ephemeral UDP ports (`127.0.0.1:0`) and dials whatever address a peer offers, so neither a port nor a host list can describe it; the only *named* outbound is the holiday source. sys=networkInterfaces: the address a device dials is this machine's LAN address, and finding it is the whole of what `sys` is for here. ffi=./node_modules: two dependencies load native libraries (node-datachannel, @infisical/quic), and the platform suffix in their paths differs per machine, so the tree is the narrowest portable scope. No `--allow-env` and no `--allow-run`: the server reads neither. A `--data` elsewhere needs the read and write flags to name it -- see `tools/serverFlags.mjs` and the message `server/main.ts` prints when it cannot reach its own directory.
tasks.//seed: 27.25 -- the fixture writer touches one directory and reads one variable. `WORKLOG_SEED_PROMPT_MS` is the journey's knob for a prompt that fires while it is watching; naming it rather than allowing `--allow-env` means a dependency that starts reading the environment is a failure rather than a surprise. Pass a directory as the argument, and give the read and write flags the same one.
tasks.//web: The trailing `--` is npm's, not a typo: without it `deno task web --host 0.0.0.0` drops the flag and vite still prints "use --host to expose". With it, every vite flag forwards (27.27). **Do not add a second one.** `deno task` passes a literal `--` through as an argument, so `deno task web -- --host 0.0.0.0` reaches vite as `-- --host 0.0.0.0`; vite reads the bare `--` as the end of its options, ignores the flag, binds to localhost and prints a normal banner with no Network line. Verified both ways rather than reasoned about -- the failing form is the one that looks right.
tasks.//test:bundle: Runs *after* web:build in the gate, never as part of `test`. It reads web/dist, so running it first checks whichever bundle happened to be lying around -- and on a fresh clone there is none, and it would skip in silence.
tasks.journey: cd web && npm run build && cd .. && node tools/journey.mjs
tasks.shots: cd web && npm run build && cd .. && node tools/screenshots.mjs
tasks.desktop:check: deno task web:build && deno desktop --backend webview --allow-read --allow-write --allow-env=HOME,USERPROFILE,XDG_CONFIG_HOME --exclude node_modules --exclude web/node_modules --include web/dist -o worklog-check desktop/selftest.ts && ./worklog-check/worklog-check
tasks.//desktop-permissions: 27.25 -- the three desktop tasks below share a permission set, and it is deliberately not `-A`. **No `--allow-net`**: the only network this process opens is the window's own, so 15.6, 15.7 and 16.3 are enforced by the runtime rather than by `desktop/main.ts` being careful. `--allow-env` names the three variables `dataDir()` reads (HOME, USERPROFILE, XDG_CONFIG_HOME) rather than the whole environment. `--allow-read`/`--allow-write` are *not* scoped, and that is a limitation rather than a decision: the paths are computed at runtime from those variables, and a flag baked into a build cannot name a directory that does not exist until it runs. A packaged app has no terminal, so a permission prompt does not fail, it hangs -- which is why these cannot be left off and discovered later.
tasks.//desktop:check: Needs a display: `xvfb-run -a deno task desktop:check` on a headless box. It verifies the bridge in `desktop/bridge.ts`, which is the only thing standing between the desktop window and a shell that silently does nothing.
tasks.desktop: deno task web:build && deno desktop --backend webview --allow-read --allow-write --allow-env=HOME,USERPROFILE,XDG_CONFIG_HOME --exclude node_modules --exclude web/node_modules --include web/dist -o worklog-dev desktop/main.ts && ./worklog-dev/worklog-dev
tasks.//desktop: `deno desktop <entry>` *builds*, it does not run. Without the `&& ./worklog-dev/worklog-dev` this task compiled an app, printed a bundle summary and exited, which reads exactly like having run it. On a headless box: `xvfb-run -a deno task desktop`.
tasks.desktop:build: deno task web:build && deno desktop --backend webview --allow-read --allow-write --allow-env=HOME,USERPROFILE,XDG_CONFIG_HOME --exclude node_modules --exclude web/node_modules --include web/dist -o Worklog desktop/main.ts
